# Docker Compose for local visual testing
docker-compose.visual-testing.yml
version: '3.8'

services:
  # Selenium Grid for cross-browser testing
  selenium-hub:
    image: selenium/hub:4.11.0
    container_name: selenium-hub
    ports:
      - "4442:4442"
      - "4443:4443"
      - "4444:4444"
    networks:
      - visual-testing

  selenium-chrome:
    image: selenium/node-chrome:4.11.0
    shm_size: 2gb
    depends_on:
      - selenium-hub
    environment:
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_HOST=selenium-hub
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_PUBLISH_PORT=4442
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_SUBSCRIBE_PORT=4443
      - SE_NODE_MAX_SESSIONS=4
      - SE_NODE_OVERRIDE_MAX_SESSIONS=true
    networks:
      - visual-testing

  selenium-firefox:
    image: selenium/node-firefox:4.11.0
    shm_size: 2gb
    depends_on:
      - selenium-hub
    environment:
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_HOST=selenium-hub
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_PUBLISH_PORT=4442
      - SE_EVENT_BUS_SUBSCRIBE_PORT=4443
    networks:
      - visual-testing

  # Applitools UFG (UltraFast Grid) for cloud testing
  applitools-ufg:
    image: applitools/ufg-container:latest
    environment:
      - APPLITOOLS_API_KEY=${APPLITOOLS_API_KEY}
      - APPLITOOLS_SERVER_URL=https://eyesapi.applitools.com
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    networks:
      - visual-testing
    volumes:
      - ./test-data/applitools:/app/data

  # Visual test runner
  test-runner:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.visual-testing
    environment:
      - NODE_ENV=test
      - TEST_ENV=${TEST_ENV:-staging}
      - APPLITOOLS_API_KEY=${APPLITOOLS_API_KEY}
      - PERCY_TOKEN=${PERCY_TOKEN}
      - SELENIUM_REMOTE_URL=http://selenium-hub:4444
      - APPLITOOLS_UFG_URL=http://applitools-ufg:80
    volumes:
      - ./features:/app/features
      - ./test-results:/app/test-results
      - ./screenshots:/app/screenshots
      - ./reports:/app/reports
    networks:
      - visual-testing
    depends_on:
      - selenium-hub
      - applitools-ufg
    command: ["npm", "run", "test:visual:docker"]

  # Test data services
  wiremock:
    image: wiremock/wiremock:latest
    ports:
      - "9090:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./test-data/wiremock:/home/wiremock
    networks:
      - visual-testing
    command: ["--global-response-templating", "--verbose"]

  test-database:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: testpass
      POSTGRES_DB: visual_test
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - ./test-data/db:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d
    networks:
      - visual-testing

  # Reporting server
  report-server:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "8081:80"
    volumes:
      - ./reports:/usr/share/nginx/html
    networks:
      - visual-testing

  # Monitoring and metrics
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:latest
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin
    volumes:
      - ./grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana
      - ./test-data/grafana-dashboards:/etc/grafana/provisioning/dashboards
    networks:
      - visual-testing

networks:
  visual-testing:
    driver: bridge

# Dockerfile for visual testing
# Dockerfile.visual-testing
FROM node:18-alpine

# Install system dependencies
RUN apk add --no-cache \
    chromium \
    nss \
    freetype \
    harfbuzz \
    ca-certificates \
    ttf-freefont \
    font-noto-ttf \
    python3 \
    make \
    g++ \
    git

# Set up Chrome for headless testing
ENV CHROME_BIN=/usr/bin/chromium-browser
ENV CHROME_PATH=/usr/lib/chromium/
ENV PUPPETEER_SKIP_CHROMIUM_DOWNLOAD=true
ENV NODE_ENV=test

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy test code and configuration
COPY features/ ./features/
COPY test-data/ ./test-data/
COPY scripts/ ./scripts/
COPY .cucumber.js ./
COPY .applitools.config.js ./

# Create non-root user
RUN addgroup -S visualtest && adduser -S visualtest -G visualtest
RUN chown -R visualtest:visualtest /app
USER visualtest

# Default command
CMD ["npm", "run", "test:visual:docker"]

content.caption: Advanced Baseline Management and Smart Comparison Engine

content.title: Optimizing Visual Test Execution Performance
content.explanation: Visual testing can become performance-intensive as test suites grow. Optimizing execution involves strategies for parallelization, selective testing, intelligent batching, and resource management. Key considerations include reducing unnecessary screenshots, optimizing comparison algorithms, implementing efficient baseline management, and leveraging cloud infrastructure for distributed execution. Performance bottlenecks typically occur in screenshot capture, image comparison, network latency, and storage operations.

content.title: Performance Optimization Strategies Matrix
rows: Run only visual tests for changed components/pages
Group related tests to share setup/teardown
Only capture screenshots after interactions complete
Cache baseline images, DOM snapshots, resources
Reuse browser instances across test suites
Use hardware acceleration, WebGL for image diff
Run critical paths first, non-critical async

content.caption: Intelligent Test Selection and Parallel Execution Engine

steps.title: Analyze Current Performance Bottlenecks
steps.description: Identify where your visual tests are spending the most time
steps.details: Use profiling tools to measure screenshot capture time, image comparison time, network latency, and resource consumption. Identify tests with flaky behavior causing retries. Document baseline performance metrics for comparison after optimizations.

steps.title: Implement Selective Test Execution
steps.description: Run only tests affected by code changes
steps.details: Integrate with version control to detect changed files. Map file changes to affected visual tests. Use dependency analysis to determine test scope. Implement fallback mechanisms for edge cases.

steps.title: Set Up Parallel Execution Infrastructure
steps.description: Distribute tests across multiple workers and browsers
steps.details: Configure Selenium Grid or cloud testing services. Implement worker pool with resource monitoring. Balance test distribution based on resource requirements. Handle test isolation and cleanup between parallel runs.

steps.title: Optimize Screenshot Capture and Comparison
steps.description: Reduce screenshot size and optimize comparison algorithms
steps.details: Capture only necessary viewport areas. Implement intelligent waiting for stability. Use hardware-accelerated image processing. Cache comparison results for identical screenshots.

steps.title: Implement Caching and Incremental Testing
steps.description: Cache test results and baselines to avoid redundant work
steps.details: Cache baseline images locally. Implement incremental baseline updates. Store comparison results with versioning. Invalidate cache based on dependency changes.

steps.title: Monitor and Adjust Optimization Strategies
steps.description: Continuously monitor performance and adjust strategies
steps.details: Set up performance dashboards. Track optimization effectiveness over time. Implement A/B testing for optimization strategies. Establish performance budgets and alerts.

content.title: Handling Dynamic Content and Eliminating Flaky Tests
Strategies for Stable Visual Testing with Dynamic Content
content.explanation: Dynamic content poses significant challenges for visual testing, causing false positives and flaky tests. Effective strategies involve identifying dynamic elements, implementing intelligent masking, using stable selectors, and leveraging AI-powered comparison tools. Key dynamic content types include: timestamps, user-specific data, rotating banners, live feeds, advertisements, A/B test variations, and data that changes based on external factors like stock prices or weather.

content.title: Dynamic Content Handling Techniques Comparison
rows: Consistent UI elements with dynamic content
Mark dynamic elements with data attributes
Allow minor differences up to threshold

content.caption: Comprehensive Dynamic Content Handler with AI Assistance

items.definition: The process of making dynamic content static during visual testing by mocking APIs, freezing timers, or replacing variable content with fixed values. This ensures consistent screenshots across test runs.
The state where all UI animations, transitions, and asynchronous updates have completed, and the visual presentation is no longer changing. Essential for reliable screenshot comparison.
The percentage of visual tests that produce inconsistent results across identical runs. A key metric for test suite reliability, calculated as (flaky tests / total tests) × 100%.
The principle where ignore regions defined for parent components automatically apply to child components, reducing maintenance overhead in component-based architectures.
The property where running a visual test multiple times with the same inputs produces identical results, regardless of external factors like timing or network conditions.

content.title: Combining Visual Testing with Accessibility Validation
content.explanation: Visual testing and accessibility testing are complementary disciplines that together ensure both the visual appearance and usability of applications for all users. By integrating accessibility checks into visual testing workflows, teams can catch accessibility violations that have visual manifestations, such as insufficient color contrast, improper text sizing, missing focus indicators, and layout issues that affect screen reader users. Modern visual testing tools can detect accessibility issues through AI analysis of screenshots, DOM inspection, and integration with dedicated accessibility testing libraries.

content.title: Accessibility Issues Detectable Through Visual Testing
rows: Text hard to read against background
No visible focus rings on interactive elements
Inconsistent font sizes, poor visual hierarchy

content.caption: Integrated Accessibility and Visual Testing Framework

content.title: Step-by-Step: Integrating Accessibility into Visual Testing

steps.title: Define Accessibility Requirements
steps.description: Establish which WCAG criteria are relevant for your application
steps.details: Determine compliance level (A, AA, AAA). Identify critical user journeys for accessibility testing. Document specific requirements for color contrast, text size, focus indicators, and keyboard navigation. Align with legal and organizational accessibility standards.

steps.title: Configure Accessibility Testing Tools
steps.description: Set up tools for automated accessibility detection
steps.details: Integrate axe-core or similar libraries. Configure color contrast analyzers. Set up screen reader simulation tools. Establish baseline accessibility metrics and thresholds.

steps.title: Implement Combined Test Workflows
steps.description: Create workflows that run visual and accessibility tests together
steps.details: Combine screenshot capture with DOM analysis. Implement parallel execution of accessibility checks. Create unified reporting for visual and accessibility issues. Set up failure thresholds for both test types.

steps.title: Create Accessibility-Focused Baselines
steps.description: Establish baselines that include accessibility requirements
steps.details: Capture baseline screenshots with accessibility metadata. Document expected accessibility scores. Create reference implementations for accessible components. Store accessibility requirements alongside visual baselines.

steps.title: Train Teams on Accessibility-Visual Integration
steps.description: Educate teams on interpreting combined results
steps.details: Create documentation on accessibility violations visible in screenshots. Train designers on accessible color palettes. Educate developers on focus management and semantic HTML. Establish review processes for accessibility issues.

steps.title: Monitor Accessibility Metrics Over Time
steps.description: Track accessibility improvements and regressions
steps.details: Set up dashboards for accessibility scores. Track violation trends across releases. Correlate accessibility issues with user feedback. Establish improvement goals and milestones.

content.title: Cross-Browser and Cross-Device Testing at Scale
Managing Visual Consistency Across Multiple Platforms
content.explanation: Cross-browser and cross-device visual testing ensures consistent user experiences across the diverse ecosystem of browsers, operating systems, and devices. This involves testing on different browser engines (WebKit, Gecko, Blink), various operating systems (Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, Linux), multiple device types (desktop, tablet, mobile), and different screen densities (1x, 2x, 3x). The challenges include rendering differences, CSS feature support variations, font rendering discrepancies, and hardware acceleration differences. Effective strategies involve prioritized browser matrices, responsive design testing, and intelligent comparison that accounts for acceptable platform-specific variations.

Key AI applications in visual testing include: computer vision for content understanding, natural language processing for text analysis, anomaly detection for unexpected changes, and predictive analytics for risk assessment.

# ai_visual_testing.py
# Advanced AI-powered visual testing using computer vision

import cv2
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
import pytesseract
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple, Optional
import json

class AIVisualTester:
    """
    AI-powered visual testing system combining computer vision,
    OCR, and machine learning for intelligent visual comparisons.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, config: Dict = None):
        self.config = config or {
            'model_path': './models/visual_testing_model.h5',
            'confidence_threshold': 0.85,
            'use_ocr': True,
            'use_object_detection': True,
            'enable_anomaly_detection': True,
            'text_similarity_threshold': 0.9
        }
        
        # Load ML models
        self.models = self.load_models()
        
        # Initialize anomaly detector
        self.anomaly_detector = IsolationForest(contamination=0.1, random_state=42)
        self.feature_vectors = []
        
    def load_models(self) -> Dict:
        """Load pre-trained ML models for visual testing."""
        models = {}
        
        try:
            # Load object detection model
            models['object_detector'] = self.load_object_detection_model()
            
            # Load semantic segmentation model
            models['segmenter'] = self.load_segmentation_model()
            
            # Load change classification model
            models['change_classifier'] = self.load_change_classifier()
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Warning: Could not load all models: {e}")
            
        return models
    
    def compare_with_ai(self, baseline_img: np.ndarray, 
                       current_img: np.ndarray, 
                       metadata: Dict = None) -> Dict:
        """
        Perform AI-powered comparison between baseline and current images.
        """
        results = {
            'status': 'unknown',
            'differences': [],
            'confidence': 0.0,
            'ai_analysis': {},
            'recommendations': []
        }
        
        # 1. Basic structural comparison
        structural_diff = self.compare_structural(baseline_img, current_img)
        results['structural_difference'] = structural_diff
        
        # 2. Object detection and comparison
        if self.config['use_object_detection'] and 'object_detector' in self.models:
            object_results = self.compare_objects(baseline_img, current_img)
            results['object_comparison'] = object_results
            results['differences'].extend(object_results.get('differences', []))
        
        # 3. Text content comparison using OCR
        if self.config['use_ocr']:
            text_results = self.compare_text_content(baseline_img, current_img)
            results['text_comparison'] = text_results
            
            # Add text differences if significant
            if text_results['similarity'] < self.config['text_similarity_threshold']:
                results['differences'].append({
                    'type': 'text_change',
                    'confidence': 1 - text_results['similarity'],
                    'details': text_results
                })
        
        # 4. Semantic segmentation for understanding regions
        if 'segmenter' in self.models:
            semantic_results = self.compare_semantic(baseline_img, current_img)
            results['semantic_comparison'] = semantic_results
            
            # Detect region changes
            region_changes = self.detect_region_changes(semantic_results)
            if region_changes:
                results['differences'].extend(region_changes)
        
        # 5. Classify changes using ML model
        if 'change_classifier' in self.models:
            change_classification = self.classify_changes(
                baseline_img, current_img, results['differences']
            )
            results['change_classification'] = change_classification
            
            # Update status based on classification
            if change_classification['is_intentional']:
                results['status'] = 'approved_change'
                results['confidence'] = change_classification['confidence']
            elif change_classification['is_bug']:
                results['status'] = 'bug_detected'
                results['confidence'] = change_classification['confidence']
        
        # 6. Anomaly detection
        if self.config['enable_anomaly_detection']:
            anomaly_result = self.detect_anomaly(results)
            if anomaly_result['is_anomaly']:
                results['status'] = 'anomaly_detected'
                results['anomaly_analysis'] = anomaly_result
        
        # 7. Generate recommendations
        results['recommendations'] = self.generate_recommendations(results)
        
        # Determine final status
        if results['status'] == 'unknown':
            if len(results['differences']) == 0:
                results['status'] = 'identical'
            else:
                results['status'] = 'differences_found'
        
        return results
    
    def compare_structural(self, img1: np.ndarray, img2: np.ndarray) -> Dict:
        """Compare structural similarity using SSIM and feature matching."""
        # Convert to grayscale for structural comparison
        gray1 = cv2.cvtColor(img1, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
        gray2 = cv2.cvtColor(img2, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
        
        # Calculate Structural Similarity Index
        from skimage.metrics import structural_similarity as ssim
        ssim_score, diff = ssim(gray1, gray2, full=True)
        
        # Feature matching
        orb = cv2.ORB_create()
        kp1, des1 = orb.detectAndCompute(gray1, None)
        kp2, des2 = orb.detectAndCompute(gray2, None)
        
        if des1 is not None and des2 is not None:
            bf = cv2.BFMatcher(cv2.NORM_HAMMING, crossCheck=True)
            matches = bf.match(des1, des2)
            match_score = len(matches) / max(len(kp1), len(kp2))
        else:
            match_score = 0
        
        return {
            'ssim': float(ssim_score),
            'feature_match': float(match_score),
            'diff_image': diff.tolist() if diff is not None else None
        }
    
    def compare_objects(self, img1: np.ndarray, img2: np.ndarray) -> Dict:
        """Detect and compare UI objects in images."""
        # This would use a pre-trained object detection model
        # For UI elements like buttons, inputs, navigation, etc.
        
        # Mock implementation
        objects1 = self.detect_ui_objects(img1)
        objects2 = self.detect_ui_objects(img2)
        
        differences = []
        
        # Compare objects
        for obj1 in objects1:
            matching_obj = self.find_matching_object(obj1, objects2)
            if matching_obj:
                # Check for visual differences
                if self.objects_differ(obj1, matching_obj):
                    differences.append({
                        'type': 'object_change',
                        'object': obj1['label'],
                        'difference': 'visual_appearance_changed',
                        'confidence': 0.85
                    })
            else:
                differences.append({
                    'type': 'object_missing',
                    'object': obj1['label'],
                    'difference': 'object_missing_in_current',
                    'confidence': 0.95
                })
        
        # Check for new objects
        for obj2 in objects2:
            if not self.find_matching_object(obj2, objects1):
                differences.append({
                    'type': 'object_added',
                    'object': obj2['label'],
                    'difference': 'new_object_detected',
                    'confidence': 0.95
                })
        
        return {
            'objects_baseline': objects1,
            'objects_current': objects2,
            'differences': differences,
            'object_count_changed': len(objects1) != len(objects2)
        }
    
    def compare_text_content(self, img1: np.ndarray, img2: np.ndarray) -> Dict:
        """Extract and compare text content using OCR."""
        # Extract text using Tesseract
        text1 = pytesseract.image_to_string(img1)
        text2 = pytesseract.image_to_string(img2)
        
        # Calculate similarity
        similarity = self.calculate_text_similarity(text1, text2)
        
        # Extract text regions
        boxes1 = pytesseract.image_to_boxes(img1)
        boxes2 = pytesseract.image_to_boxes(img2)
        
        return {
            'text_baseline': text1,
            'text_current': text2,
            'similarity': similarity,
            'boxes_baseline': boxes1,
            'boxes_current': boxes2,
            'significant_change': similarity < self.config['text_similarity_threshold']
        }
    
    def compare_semantic(self, img1: np.ndarray, img2: np.ndarray) -> Dict:
        """Compare semantic regions using segmentation."""
        # Segment images into semantic regions
        # (text regions, buttons, images, background, etc.)
        
        segments1 = self.segment_image(img1)
        segments2 = self.segment_image(img2)
        
        return {
            'segments_baseline': segments1,
            'segments_current': segments2,
            'segment_count': len(segments1),
            'segment_changes': self.compare_segments(segments1, segments2)
        }
    
    def classify_changes(self, img1: np.ndarray, img2: np.ndarray, 
                        differences: List) -> Dict:
        """Classify changes as intentional or bugs using ML."""
        # Extract features for classification
        features = self.extract_change_features(img1, img2, differences)
        
        # Use pre-trained model to classify
        if 'change_classifier' in self.models:
            prediction = self.models['change_classifier'].predict([features])
            confidence = np.max(prediction)
            class_idx = np.argmax(prediction)
            
            # Class mapping: 0=bug, 1=intentional, 2=cosmetic
            classes = ['bug', 'intentional', 'cosmetic']
            
            return {
                'classification': classes[class_idx],
                'confidence': float(confidence),
                'is_bug': class_idx == 0,
                'is_intentional': class_idx == 1,
                'is_cosmetic': class_idx == 2,
                'features_used': len(features)
            }
        
        # Fallback heuristic classification
        return self.heuristic_classification(differences)
    
    def detect_anomaly(self, comparison_results: Dict) -> Dict:
        """Detect anomalous patterns in comparison results."""
        # Extract features for anomaly detection
        features = self.extract_anomaly_features(comparison_results)
        self.feature_vectors.append(features)
        
        if len(self.feature_vectors) > 10:
            # Fit anomaly detector
            self.anomaly_detector.fit(self.feature_vectors)
            
            # Predict anomaly
            is_anomaly = self.anomaly_detector.predict([features])[0] == -1
            anomaly_score = self.anomaly_detector.decision_function([features])[0]
            
            return {
                'is_anomaly': bool(is_anomaly),
                'anomaly_score': float(anomaly_score),
                'features': features.tolist() if hasattr(features, 'tolist') else features
            }
        
        return {'is_anomaly': False, 'anomaly_score': 0.0}
    
    # Helper methods
    def calculate_text_similarity(self, text1: str, text2: str) -> float:
        """Calculate similarity between two text strings."""
        return SequenceMatcher(None, text1, text2).ratio()
    
    def detect_ui_objects(self, img: np.ndarray) -> List[Dict]:
        """Detect UI objects in image (mock implementation)."""
        # In real implementation, use object detection model
        # trained on UI components
        return []
    
    def segment_image(self, img: np.ndarray) -> List[Dict]:
        """Segment image into semantic regions (mock)."""
        return []
    
    def extract_change_features(self, img1: np.ndarray, img2: np.ndarray, 
                              differences: List) -> np.ndarray:
        """Extract features for change classification."""
        # Extract various features for ML classification
        features = []
        
        # Number of differences
        features.append(len(differences))
        
        # Types of differences
        diff_types = [d.get('type', 'unknown') for d in differences]
        features.extend([
            diff_types.count('text_change'),
            diff_types.count('object_change'),
            diff_types.count('object_missing'),
            diff_types.count('object_added')
        ])
        
        # Structural features
        structural = self.compare_structural(img1, img2)
        features.append(structural['ssim'])
        features.append(structural['feature_match'])
        
        return np.array(features)
    
    def heuristic_classification(self, differences: List) -> Dict:
        """Heuristic classification of changes."""
        if not differences:
            return {
                'classification': 'identical',
                'confidence': 1.0,
                'is_bug': False,
                'is_intentional': False,
                'is_cosmetic': False
            }
        
        # Simple heuristic based on difference types
        diff_types = [d.get('type', 'unknown') for d in differences]
        
        if 'object_missing' in diff_types:
            return {
                'classification': 'bug',
                'confidence': 0.8,
                'is_bug': True,
                'is_intentional': False,
                'is_cosmetic': False
            }
        elif all(t in ['text_change', 'cosmetic'] for t in diff_types):
            return {
                'classification': 'cosmetic',
                'confidence': 0.7,
                'is_bug': False,
                'is_intentional': False,
                'is_cosmetic': True
            }
        else:
            return {
                'classification': 'intentional',
                'confidence': 0.6,
                'is_bug': False,
                'is_intentional': True,
                'is_cosmetic': False
            }
    
    def generate_recommendations(self, results: Dict) -> List[str]:
        """Generate recommendations based on analysis results."""
        recommendations = []
        
        if results['status'] == 'bug_detected':
            recommendations.append("Review detected bugs before deployment")
            
        if results.get('text_comparison', {}).get('significant_change', False):
            recommendations.append("Verify text content changes are intentional")
            
        if results.get('object_comparison', {}).get('object_count_changed', False):
            recommendations.append("Check for missing or added UI components")
            
        if results.get('anomaly_analysis', {}).get('is_anomaly', False):
            recommendations.append("Unusual pattern detected - manual review recommended")
            
        return recommendations

# Integration with testing framework
class AIVisualTestingPipeline:
    """Orchestrates AI-powered visual testing workflow."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.ai_tester = AIVisualTester()
        self.history = []
        
    async def test_page(self, url: str, test_name: str, baseline_img: np.ndarray = None):
        """Test a page with AI-powered visual testing."""
        # Capture current screenshot
        current_img = await self.capture_screenshot(url)
        
        # Load baseline if not provided

        results = self.ai_tester.compare_with_ai(baseline_img, current_img, {
            'test_name': test_name,
            'url': url,

        })
        
        # Store results
        self.history.append({
            'test_name': test_name,
            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'results': results
        })
        
        # Generate report
        report = self.generate_report(results)
        
        # Update baseline if changes are approved
        if results['status'] in ['approved_change', 'cosmetic']:
            self.update_baseline(test_name, current_img, results)
        
        return results, report
    
    def generate_report(self, results: Dict) -> str:
        """Generate human-readable report."""
        report = f"""
AI Visual Testing Report
=======================

"""
        
        if results['differences']:

            for diff in results['differences']:
                report += f"- {diff.get('type', 'unknown')}: {diff.get('difference', 'N/A')}\n"
        else:
            report += "No significant differences found\n"
        
        if results.get('change_classification'):
            classification = results['change_classification']
            report += f"\nChange Classification: {classification['classification']}\n"
            report += f"Confidence: {classification['confidence']:.2%}\n"
        
        if results.get('recommendations'):
            report += "\nRecommendations:\n"

content.title: Understanding Self-Healing Test Automation
content.explanation: Self-healing test automation refers to the ability of test scripts to automatically adapt to changes in the application under test, particularly changes to the user interface. Traditional test automation suffers from brittle locators that break when developers change HTML structure, CSS classes, or element IDs. Self-healing automation uses artificial intelligence to create resilient locators, detect when elements change, and automatically find alternative ways to interact with the application. This approach significantly reduces test maintenance overhead and improves test stability in dynamic development environments.

steps.title: Define Multiple Identification Strategies
steps.description: Create comprehensive element identification using multiple attributes
steps.details: Instead of relying on a single locator (like ID or XPath), capture multiple identification attributes for each element: ID, CSS class, XPath, text content, relative position, visual characteristics, and semantic context. Store these attributes in a structured format that allows fallback strategies when primary locators fail.

steps.title: Implement Dynamic Element Rediscovery
steps.description: Build algorithms to find elements when original locators fail
steps.details: When a locator fails, implement search algorithms that try alternative attributes. Use semantic similarity to find elements with similar text or functionality. Employ visual recognition to find elements that look similar. Leverage DOM structure analysis to find elements in similar positions relative to stable anchor elements.

steps.title: Create Learning and Adaptation Mechanisms
steps.description: Enable the system to learn from successful recoveries
steps.details: Track which locator strategies work best for different types of elements and pages. Use machine learning to predict which attributes are most stable for specific UI patterns. Automatically update locator strategies based on historical success rates. Implement confidence scoring for different identification methods.

steps.title: Integrate Computer Vision for Visual Recognition
steps.description: Add visual element recognition as a fallback strategy
steps.details: Capture visual signatures of important elements during test creation. Use template matching and feature detection algorithms to find elements visually. Implement OCR to read text from screenshots when DOM-based text extraction fails. Combine visual recognition with semantic understanding for robust element identification.

steps.title: Build Context-Aware Recovery Strategies
steps.description: Implement intelligent recovery based on page context
steps.details: Analyze the page structure and flow to understand what elements should be present. Use business logic and user journey understanding to predict expected elements. Implement recovery strategies tailored to specific failure patterns (login failures, navigation issues, form submission problems).

import numpy as np
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from selenium.webdriver.remote.webelement import WebElement
from typing import List, Dict, Optional
import cv2
import pytesseract

class AISelfHealingLocator:
    """
    Advanced self-healing locator system that uses multiple AI techniques
    to maintain test stability in dynamic web applications.
    
    Features:
    - Multi-attribute element identification
    - Visual element recognition fallback
    - Semantic similarity matching
    - Machine learning for locator strategy selection
    - Automatic locator updates
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.element_features = {}
        self.ml_model = self._train_locator_model()
        self.fallback_strategies = [
            self._find_by_visual_similarity,
            self._find_by_semantic_similarity,
            self._find_by_structural_context,
            self._find_by_relative_position
        ]
        
        # Track locator performance for continuous learning
        self.locator_performance = {
            'success_count': {},
            'failure_count': {},
            'recovery_patterns': []
        }
    
    def create_smart_locator(self, element: WebElement) -> Dict:
        """
        Create a comprehensive locator with multiple identification strategies.
        
        This method captures multiple attributes and creates fallback strategies
        to ensure the element can be found even if some attributes change.
        """
        
        locator = {
            'primary': self._get_best_locator(element),
            'fallbacks': self._get_fallback_locators(element),
            'visual_signature': self._capture_visual_signature(element),
            'semantic_features': self._extract_semantic_features(element),
            'structural_context': self._get_structural_context(element),
            'stability_score': self._calculate_stability_score(element),
            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        # Store for future reference and learning
        element_id = self._generate_element_id(element)
        self.element_features[element_id] = {
            'locator': locator,
            'features': self._extract_element_features(element)
        }
        
        return locator
    
    def find_element_with_healing(self, driver, original_locator: Dict, 
                                 context: Dict = None) -> Optional[WebElement]:
        """
        Find an element using self-healing capabilities.
        
        This method attempts multiple strategies to find the element:
        1. Try the primary locator
        2. Try fallback locators
        3. Use AI-powered recovery strategies
        4. Learn from successful recoveries
        """
        
        start_time = time.time()
        recovery_attempts = []
        
        try:
            # Step 1: Try primary locator first
            element = self._find_with_locator(driver, original_locator['primary'])
            if element:
                self._record_success('primary', original_locator['primary'])
                return element
        except Exception as e:
            recovery_attempts.append({
                'strategy': 'primary',
                'error': str(e),
                'duration': time.time() - start_time
            })
        
        # Step 2: Try fallback locators
        for i, fallback in enumerate(original_locator['fallbacks']):
            try:
                element = self._find_with_locator(driver, fallback)
                if element:
                    # Update the locator for future use
                    self._update_locator_success_rate(original_locator['primary'], False)
                    self._update_locator_success_rate(fallback, True)
                    
                    # Suggest updating the primary locator
                    self._suggest_locator_update(original_locator, fallback)
                    
                    return element
            except Exception as e:
                recovery_attempts.append({
                    'strategy': f'fallback_{i}',
                    'error': str(e),
                    'duration': time.time() - start_time
                })
                continue
        
        # Step 3: Try AI-powered recovery strategies
        for strategy in self.fallback_strategies:
            try:
                element = strategy(driver, original_locator, context)
                if element:
                    # Learn from successful recovery
                    self._learn_recovery_pattern(original_locator, strategy.__name__)
                    
                    # Create new locator for the found element
                    new_locator = self.create_smart_locator(element)
                    self._suggest_locator_update(original_locator, new_locator)
                    
                    return element
            except Exception as e:
                recovery_attempts.append({
                    'strategy': strategy.__name__,
                    'error': str(e),
                    'duration': time.time() - start_time
                })
                continue
        
        # Step 4: Log failure for analysis
        self._record_failure(original_locator, recovery_attempts)
        
        # Step 5: Generate suggestions for manual intervention
        suggestions = self._generate_recovery_suggestions(original_locator, recovery_attempts)
        
        return None
    
    def _find_by_visual_similarity(self, driver, original_locator: Dict, 
                                 context: Dict = None) -> Optional[WebElement]:
        """
        Use computer vision to find visually similar elements.
        
        This method:
        1. Captures a screenshot of the current page
        2. Uses template matching to find the visual signature
        3. Converts screen coordinates to DOM elements
        4. Verifies the element semantics match expectations
        """
        
        # Capture current page screenshot
        screenshot = driver.get_screenshot_as_png()
        
        # Convert to OpenCV format
        nparr = np.frombuffer(screenshot, np.uint8)
        current_screen = cv2.imdecode(nparr, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
        
        # Load original visual signature
        original_signature = original_locator['visual_signature']
        
        # Template matching with multiple methods for robustness
        methods = [cv2.TM_CCOEFF_NORMED, cv2.TM_CCORR_NORMED]
        best_match = None
        best_confidence = 0
        
        for method in methods:
            result = cv2.matchTemplate(current_screen, original_signature, method)
            min_val, max_val, min_loc, max_loc = cv2.minMaxLoc(result)
            
            if max_val > best_confidence:
                best_confidence = max_val
                best_match = max_loc if method in [cv2.TM_CCOEFF_NORMED, cv2.TM_CCORR_NORMED] else min_loc
        
        if best_confidence > 0.8:  # Confidence threshold
            # Convert template matching result to element coordinates
            x, y = best_match
            w, h = original_signature.shape[1], original_signature.shape[0]
            
            # Use JavaScript to find element at coordinates
            script = f"""
            var element = document.elementFromPoint({x + w//2}, {y + h//2});
            // Walk up the DOM tree to find a clickable element
            while (element && 
                   (element.nodeType !== 1 || 
                    (element.tagName.toLowerCase() === 'body' && 
                     element.parentElement))) {{
                element = element.parentElement;
            }}
            return element;
            """
            element = driver.execute_script(script)
            
            if element and self._verify_element_semantics(element, original_locator):
                return element
        
        return None
    
    def _find_by_semantic_similarity(self, driver, original_locator: Dict, 
                                   context: Dict = None) -> Optional[WebElement]:
        """
        Find elements with similar semantic meaning using NLP techniques.
        
        This method understands what an element DOES rather than just what it looks like.
        For example, it can find a 'Submit' button even if the text changes to 'Send'.
        """
        
        target_features = original_locator['semantic_features']
        all_elements = driver.find_elements("xpath", "//*[not(self::script) and not(self::style)]")
        
        best_match = None
        best_score = 0
        
        for element in all_elements:
            try:
                current_features = self._extract_semantic_features(element)
                similarity_score = self._calculate_semantic_similarity(
                    target_features, current_features
                )
                
                # Consider element visibility and interactability
                if (similarity_score > best_score and 
                    similarity_score > 0.7 and
                    element.is_displayed() and
                    element.is_enabled()):
                    best_score = similarity_score
                    best_match = element
            except Exception:
                continue
        
        return best_match
    
    def _calculate_semantic_similarity(self, features1: Dict, features2: Dict) -> float:
        """Calculate semantic similarity between two elements"""
        
        score = 0
        total_weight = 0
        
        # Compare text content using NLP similarity
        if features1.get('text') and features2.get('text'):
            text_sim = self._text_similarity(features1['text'], features2['text'])
            score += text_sim * 0.3
            total_weight += 0.3
        
        # Compare element type and role
        if features1.get('tag') == features2.get('tag'):
            score += 0.2
            total_weight += 0.2
        
        # Compare ARIA roles and attributes
        aria_similarity = self._aria_similarity(
            features1.get('aria_attributes', {}),
            features2.get('aria_attributes', {})
        )
        score += aria_similarity * 0.2
        total_weight += 0.2
        
        # Compare interaction patterns
        interaction_similarity = self._interaction_similarity(
            features1.get('interaction_type', ''),
            features2.get('interaction_type', '')
        )
        score += interaction_similarity * 0.3
        total_weight += 0.3
        
        return score / total_weight if total_weight > 0 else 0
    
    def _train_locator_model(self):
        """
        Train ML model to predict best locator strategies.
        
        This model learns which locator strategies work best for different
        types of elements based on historical performance data.
        """
        
        # Feature engineering for ML model
        features = [
            'element_complexity',      # How complex is the element's HTML structure
            'page_volatility',         # How often does this page change
            'test_frequency',          # How often is this test run
            'element_type',            # Button, input, link, etc.
            'application_area',        # Login, checkout, dashboard, etc.
            'development_phase',       # Early dev, testing, production
            'change_history'           # Historical frequency of changes
        ]
        
        # Target: locator_success_rate
        model = RandomForestClassifier(
            n_estimators=100,
            max_depth=10,
            random_state=42
        )
        
        # Load historical training data
        # In practice, this would come from a database of past test executions
        # training_data = self._load_training_data()
        # model.fit(training_data['features'], training_data['target'])
        
        return model
    
    def predict_best_locator_strategy(self, element_features: Dict) -> str:
        """
        Predict the most reliable locator strategy for an element.
        
        Uses the trained ML model to recommend which identification method
        (ID, XPath, CSS, visual, semantic) is likely to be most stable.
        """
        
        features = self._extract_ml_features(element_features)
        prediction = self.ml_model.predict([features])
        
        strategies = ['id', 'xpath', 'css', 'visual', 'semantic', 'hybrid']
        return strategies[prediction[0]]

class IntelligentTestRecovery:
    """
    Advanced test recovery system that learns from failures
    and suggests optimal recovery strategies.
    
    This system:
    - Analyzes failure patterns across test executions
    - Suggests context-aware recovery strategies
    - Learns from successful recovery attempts
    - Predicts likely failures before they occur
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.test_execution_history = {}
        self.failure_patterns = {}
        self.recovery_success_rates = {}
        self.prediction_model = self._build_prediction_model()
    
    def analyze_failure_patterns(self, test_results: List[Dict]):
        """
        Analyze test failures to identify patterns and root causes.
        
        This method clusters similar failures and identifies:
        - Common failure times (e.g., after deployments)
        - Related test failures (e.g., all checkout tests failing)
        - Environmental factors (e.g., browser-specific issues)
        - Application change patterns (e.g., UI refactoring periods)
        """
        
        for result in test_results:
            if result['status'] == 'FAILED':
                failure_signature = self._create_failure_signature(result)
                
                if failure_signature in self.failure_patterns:
                    self.failure_patterns[failure_signature]['count'] += 1
                    self.failure_patterns[failure_signature]['recent_timestamps'].append(
                        result['timestamp']
                    )
                    
                    # Update patterns based on new failure
                    self._update_failure_pattern(failure_signature, result)
                else:
                    self.failure_patterns[failure_signature] = {
                        'count': 1,
                        'first_occurrence': result['timestamp'],
                        'recent_timestamps': [result['timestamp']],
                        'error_type': result['error_type'],
                        'error_message': result['error_message'],
                        'test_context': result.get('context', {}),
                        'environment': result.get('environment', {}),
                        'recovery_attempts': [],
                        'root_cause_analysis': self._analyze_root_cause(result)
                    }
        
        # Identify emerging patterns
        self._identify_emerging_patterns()
        
        # Generate preventive recommendations
        recommendations = self._generate_preventive_recommendations()
        return recommendations
    
    def suggest_recovery_strategy(self, failure_signature: str, 
                                context: Dict = None) -> Dict:
        """
        Suggest optimal recovery strategy based on failure patterns.
        
        Considers:
        - Historical success rates of different strategies
        - Current application state
        - Test execution context
        - Time constraints
        """
        
        pattern = self.failure_patterns.get(failure_signature, {})
        
        # Check for known patterns with high success rates
        if pattern.get('count', 0) > 3:
            # Frequent failure - analyze pattern
            if self._is_timing_related(pattern):
                return {
                    'strategy': 'timing_adjustment',
                    'confidence': 0.85,
                    'actions': [
                        'increase_wait_times',
                        'add_explicit_waits',
                        'implement_retry_with_backoff',
                        'check_application_performance'
                    ],
                    'estimated_success_rate': 0.9,
                    'expected_duration': '30 seconds'
                }
            elif 'element_not_found' in pattern.get('error_type', ''):
                # Element location issue
                return {
                    'strategy': 'element_recovery',
                    'confidence': 0.8,
                    'actions': [
                        'self_healing_locators',
                        'visual_element_detection',
                        'alternative_interaction_path',
                        'page_refresh_and_retry'
                    ],
                    'estimated_success_rate': 0.75,
                    'expected_duration': '45 seconds'
                }
            elif 'timeout' in pattern.get('error_type', '').lower():
                # Timeout issues
                return {
                    'strategy': 'timeout_optimization',
                    'confidence': 0.9,
                    'actions': [
                        'increase_timeout_values',
                        'optimize_test_data',
                        'check_network_conditions',
                        'verify_backend_services'
                    ],
                    'estimated_success_rate': 0.85,
                    'expected_duration': '60 seconds'
                }
        
        # Default intelligent recovery strategy
        return {
            'strategy': 'intelligent_recovery',
            'confidence': 0.7,
            'actions': [
                'analyze_current_state',
                'try_alternative_workflow',
                'check_application_health',
                'fallback_to_manual_verification'
            ],
            'estimated_success_rate': 0.65,
            'expected_duration': '90 seconds',
            'monitoring_suggestions': self._generate_monitoring_suggestions(context)
        }
    
    def learn_from_recovery(self, failure_signature: str, strategy: str, 
                          success: bool, metrics: Dict = None):
        """
        Learn from recovery attempts to improve future suggestions.
        
        This method:
        - Updates success rates for different strategies
        - Identifies strategy effectiveness in different contexts
        - Builds a knowledge base for future recommendations
        - Adjusts confidence scores based on real outcomes
        """
        
        if failure_signature not in self.recovery_success_rates:
            self.recovery_success_rates[failure_signature] = {}
        
        if strategy not in self.recovery_success_rates[failure_signature]:
            self.recovery_success_rates[failure_signature][strategy] = {
                'attempts': 0,
                'successes': 0,
                'average_duration': 0,
                'contexts': []
            }
        
        record = self.recovery_success_rates[failure_signature][strategy]
        record['attempts'] += 1
        
        if success:
            record['successes'] += 1
            
            # Update average duration
            if metrics and 'duration' in metrics:
                total_duration = record['average_duration'] * (record['attempts'] - 1)
                record['average_duration'] = (total_duration + metrics['duration']) / record['attempts']
            
            # Store context information for pattern learning
            if metrics and 'context' in metrics:
                record['contexts'].append(metrics['context'])
        
        # Update the prediction model with new data
        self._update_prediction_model(failure_signature, strategy, success, metrics)
        
        # If strategy is highly successful, promote it for similar failures
        success_rate = record['successes'] / record['attempts']
        if success_rate > 0.8 and record['attempts'] >= 5:
            self._promote_strategy_for_similar_failures(failure_signature, strategy)

By analyzing historical test execution data, code change patterns, and failure correlations, these systems can optimize test suites for maximum efficiency and coverage. This approach helps teams: 1) Reduce test execution time by running only necessary tests, 2) Identify high-risk areas that need more testing, 3) Detect flaky tests early, and 4) Allocate testing resources effectively. The key is moving from static test suites to dynamic, intelligent test selection based on real-time data and predictions.

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingClassifier, RandomForestRegressor
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import List, Dict, Any, Tuple
import networkx as nx

class PredictiveTestSelector:
    """
    Advanced test selection system that uses machine learning to
    optimize test execution based on risk, coverage, and efficiency.
    
    Key capabilities:
    - Risk-based test prioritization
    - Change impact analysis
    - Flaky test detection
    - Optimal test suite composition
    - Execution time optimization
    """
    
    def __init__(self, config: Dict[str, Any] = None):
        self.config = config or {
            'min_test_history': 10,
            'risk_threshold': 0.7,
            'time_budget_multiplier': 1.2,
            'parallelization_factor': 4,
            'learning_rate': 0.1
        }
        
        self.test_history = pd.DataFrame()
        self.risk_model = self._train_risk_model()
        self.flakiness_detector = FlakinessDetector()
        self.dependency_graph = nx.DiGraph()
        self.optimization_cache = {}
        
    def select_optimal_test_suite(self, code_changes: Dict[str, Any], 
                                available_time: int,
                                constraints: Dict[str, Any] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Select the optimal test suite based on multiple factors.
        
        This method:
        1. Identifies tests affected by code changes
        2. Calculates risk scores for each test
        3. Applies constraints (time, resources, coverage)
        4. Optimizes for maximum risk coverage
        5. Generates execution plan
        """
        
        analysis_start = datetime.now()
        
        # Step 1: Get all potentially affected tests
        affected_tests = self._get_affected_tests(code_changes)
        
        if not affected_tests:
            return {
                'selected_tests': [],
                'reasoning': 'No tests affected by changes',
                'risk_coverage': 0,
                'estimated_time': 0
            }
        
        # Step 2: Calculate comprehensive risk scores
        risk_scores = self._calculate_risk_scores(affected_tests, code_changes)
        
        # Step 3: Apply business constraints
        constraints = constraints or {}
        filtered_tests = self._apply_constraints(risk_scores, constraints)
        
        # Step 4: Prioritize tests based on risk and time
        prioritized_tests = self._prioritize_by_risk_and_time(
            filtered_tests, 
            available_time,
            constraints.get('parallel_execution', True)
        )
        
        # Step 5: Generate execution plan
        execution_plan = self._generate_execution_plan(
            prioritized_tests, 
            available_time,
            constraints
        )
        
        analysis_duration = (datetime.now() - analysis_start).total_seconds()
        
        return {
            'selected_tests': prioritized_tests,
            'execution_plan': execution_plan,
            'analysis_metrics': {
                'total_tests_considered': len(affected_tests),
                'selected_test_count': len(prioritized_tests),
                'risk_coverage': self._calculate_risk_coverage(prioritized_tests, risk_scores),
                'time_utilization': execution_plan['time_utilization'],
                'parallel_efficiency': execution_plan['parallel_efficiency'],
                'analysis_duration': analysis_duration
            },
            'recommendations': self._generate_recommendations(prioritized_tests, risk_scores)
        }
    
    def _get_affected_tests(self, code_changes: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[str]:
        """
        Determine which tests are affected by code changes using multiple methods.
        
        Methods include:
        1. Direct file-to-test mapping
        2. Dependency analysis
        3. Historical correlation
        4. Semantic code analysis
        """
        
        affected_tests = set()
        
        # Method 1: Direct file mapping
        for file_path in code_changes.get('modified_files', []):
            file_tests = self._map_file_to_tests(file_path)
            affected_tests.update(file_tests)
        
        # Method 2: Dependency analysis
        dependency_tests = self._find_dependency_affected_tests(code_changes)
        affected_tests.update(dependency_tests)
        
        # Method 3: Historical correlation
        historical_tests = self._find_historically_affected_tests(code_changes)
        affected_tests.update(historical_tests)
        
        # Method 4: Business logic analysis
        business_tests = self._find_business_affected_tests(code_changes)
        affected_tests.update(business_tests)
        
        return list(affected_tests)
    
    def _calculate_risk_scores(self, test_list: List[str], 
                             code_changes: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]:
        """
        Calculate multi-dimensional risk scores for each test.
        
        Risk dimensions:
        1. Historical failure probability
        2. Code change impact
        3. Business criticality
        4. Test stability (flakiness)
        5. Execution environment risk
        """
        
        risk_scores = {}
        
        for test_name in test_list:
            scores = {}
            
            # Dimension 1: Historical failure rate
            historical_data = self._get_test_history(test_name)
            if not historical_data.empty:
                failure_rate = len(historical_data[historical_data['status'] == 'FAILED']) / len(historical_data)
                scores['historical_risk'] = failure_rate
            else:
                scores['historical_risk'] = 0.5  # Default for new tests
            
            # Dimension 2: Code change impact
            change_impact = self._calculate_change_impact(test_name, code_changes)
            scores['change_impact_risk'] = change_impact
            
            # Dimension 3: Business criticality
            business_criticality = self._get_business_criticality(test_name)
            scores['business_risk'] = business_criticality
            
            # Dimension 4: Test stability
            flakiness_score = self.flakiness_detector.get_flakiness_score(test_name)
            scores['stability_risk'] = flakiness_score
            
            # Dimension 5: Environmental risk
            environmental_risk = self._calculate_environmental_risk(test_name)
            scores['environmental_risk'] = environmental_risk
            
            # Combined risk score (weighted average)
            weights = {
                'historical_risk': 0.25,
                'change_impact_risk': 0.35,
                'business_risk': 0.20,
                'stability_risk': 0.10,
                'environmental_risk': 0.10
            }
            
            total_score = sum(scores[dim] * weights[dim] for dim in scores)
            
            risk_scores[test_name] = {
                'total_score': total_score,
                'dimension_scores': scores,
                'weights': weights,
                'execution_time': self._get_test_execution_time(test_name),
                'last_execution': self._get_last_execution_time(test_name)
            }
        
        return risk_scores
    
    def _prioritize_by_risk_and_time(self, risk_scores: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]], 
                                   available_minutes: int,
                                   parallel_execution: bool = True) -> List[str]:
        """
        Select tests that maximize risk coverage within time constraints.
        
        This is essentially a knapsack problem with additional constraints:
        - Tests have different execution times
        - Tests have different risk scores
        - Some tests have dependencies
        - Parallel execution capability
        """
        
        # Convert to seconds
        available_seconds = available_minutes * 60
        
        # Get test execution times
        test_names = list(risk_scores.keys())
        test_times = {name: risk_scores[name]['execution_time'] for name in test_names}
        test_risks = {name: risk_scores[name]['total_score'] for name in test_names}
        
        if parallel_execution:
            # Parallel execution allows grouping tests
            return self._optimize_parallel_execution(
                test_names, test_risks, test_times, available_seconds
            )
        else:
            # Sequential execution - classic knapsack
            return self._optimize_sequential_execution(
                test_names, test_risks, test_times, available_seconds
            )
    
    def _optimize_parallel_execution(self, test_names: List[str], 
                                   test_risks: Dict[str, float],
                                   test_times: Dict[str, float],
                                   available_seconds: int) -> List[str]:
        """
        Optimize test selection for parallel execution.
        
        This algorithm:
        1. Groups tests by execution time
        2. Balances load across parallel workers
        3. Maximizes risk coverage per time unit
        4. Considers test dependencies
        """
        
        max_parallel = self.config['parallelization_factor']
        
        # Sort tests by risk/time ratio (efficiency)
        test_efficiency = {}
        for test_name in test_names:
            efficiency = test_risks[test_name] / test_times[test_name]
            test_efficiency[test_name] = efficiency
        
        # Sort by efficiency (descending)
        sorted_tests = sorted(test_names, 
                            key=lambda x: test_efficiency[x], 
                            reverse=True)
        
        # Create buckets for parallel execution
        buckets = [[] for _ in range(max_parallel)]
        bucket_times = [0] * max_parallel
        
        # Distribute tests to buckets using best-fit decreasing
        for test_name in sorted_tests:
            test_time = test_times[test_name]
            
            # Find bucket with minimum load that can accommodate this test
            min_load = float('inf')
            best_bucket = 0
            
            for i in range(max_parallel):
                if bucket_times[i] + test_time <= available_seconds:
                    if bucket_times[i] < min_load:
                        min_load = bucket_times[i]
                        best_bucket = i
            
            if min_load != float('inf'):
                buckets[best_bucket].append(test_name)
                bucket_times[best_bucket] += test_time
        
        # Flatten buckets and return
        selected_tests = []
        for bucket in buckets:
            selected_tests.extend(bucket)
        
        return selected_tests
    
    def _generate_execution_plan(self, selected_tests: List[str],
                               available_time: int,
                               constraints: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Generate detailed execution plan for selected tests.
        
        The plan includes:
        - Test execution order
        - Parallel grouping
        - Time estimates
        - Resource allocation
        - Contingency plans
        """
        
        # Calculate test dependencies
        test_dependencies = self._get_test_dependencies(selected_tests)
        
        # Create execution graph
        execution_graph = self._build_execution_graph(
            selected_tests, 
            test_dependencies,
            constraints.get('parallel_execution', True)
        )
        
        # Calculate critical path
        critical_path = self._calculate_critical_path(execution_graph)
        
        # Generate timeline
        timeline = self._generate_timeline(execution_graph, available_time)
        
        # Calculate efficiency metrics
        total_execution_time = sum(
            self._get_test_execution_time(test) 
            for test in selected_tests
        )
        
        if constraints.get('parallel_execution', True):
            parallel_time = timeline['total_duration']
            parallel_efficiency = total_execution_time / (parallel_time * len(timeline['parallel_groups']))
        else:
            parallel_efficiency = 1.0
        
        return {
            'execution_order': timeline['execution_order'],
            'parallel_groups': timeline.get('parallel_groups', []),
            'critical_path': critical_path,
            'estimated_duration': timeline['total_duration'],

class FlakinessDetector:
    """
    Advanced flaky test detection using statistical analysis and ML.
    
    Detects patterns indicative of flaky tests:
    - Alternating pass/fail patterns
    - Time-based flakiness
    - Environment-dependent failures
    - Random intermittent failures
    """
    
    def __init__(self, config: Dict[str, Any] = None):
        self.config = config or {
            'flakiness_threshold': 0.1,
            'min_executions': 10,
            'pattern_window': 5,
            'environment_factors': ['browser', 'os', 'network', 'time_of_day']
        }
        
        self.pattern_detector = PatternDetector()
        self.statistical_analyzer = StatisticalAnalyzer()
        
    def detect_flaky_tests(self, test_results: pd.DataFrame) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Identify flaky tests using multiple detection methods.
        """
        
        flaky_tests = []
        
        for test_name in test_results['test_name'].unique():
            test_data = test_results[test_results['test_name'] == test_name]
            
            if len(test_data) < self.config['min_executions']:
                continue
            
            # Run multiple detection methods
            detection_results = {
                'statistical_flakiness': self._detect_statistical_flakiness(test_data),
                'pattern_flakiness': self._detect_pattern_flakiness(test_data),
                'environmental_flakiness': self._detect_environmental_flakiness(test_data),
                'timing_flakiness': self._detect_timing_flakiness(test_data)
            }
            
            # Calculate combined flakiness score
            combined_score = self._calculate_combined_score(detection_results)
            
            if combined_score > self.config['flakiness_threshold']:
                flaky_tests.append({
                    'test_name': test_name,
                    'flakiness_score': combined_score,
                    'detection_results': detection_results,
                    'execution_count': len(test_data),
                    'failure_rate': len(test_data[test_data['status'] == 'FAILED']) / len(test_data),
                    'recommendations': self._generate_flakiness_recommendations(detection_results)
                })
        
        return flaky_tests
    
    def _detect_pattern_flakiness(self, test_data: pd.DataFrame) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Detect flakiness patterns in test execution results.
        """
        
        # Sort by execution time
        test_data = test_data.sort_values('execution_time').reset_index(drop=True)
        
        patterns = {
            'alternating_pattern': self._detect_alternating_pattern(test_data),
            'clustered_failures': self._detect_clustered_failures(test_data),
            'periodic_pattern': self._detect_periodic_pattern(test_data),
            'trending_failures': self._detect_trending_failures(test_data)
        }
        
        return {
            'patterns': patterns,
            'confidence': self._calculate_pattern_confidence(patterns),
            'suggestions': self._generate_pattern_suggestions(patterns)
        }
    
    def _detect_alternating_pattern(self, test_data: pd.DataFrame) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Detect alternating pass/fail patterns"""
        
        status_changes = 0
        max_alternations = len(test_data) - 1
        
        for i in range(1, len(test_data)):
            if test_data.iloc[i]['status'] != test_data.iloc[i-1]['status']:
                status_changes += 1
        
        alternation_rate = status_changes / max_alternations if max_alternations > 0 else 0
        
        return {
            'alternation_rate': alternation_rate,
            'status_changes': status_changes,
            'is_flaky': alternation_rate > 0.5,
            'pattern_type': 'alternating' if alternation_rate > 0.5 else 'stable'
        }
    
    def _detect_environmental_flakiness(self, test_data: pd.DataFrame) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Detect flakiness related to environmental factors.
        """
        
        environmental_correlations = {}
        
        for factor in self.config['environment_factors']:
            if factor in test_data.columns:
                # Calculate failure rate by environment factor
                factor_groups = test_data.groupby(factor)['status'].apply(
                    lambda x: (x == 'FAILED').mean()
                )
                
                # Check for significant variation
                if len(factor_groups) > 1:
                    variation = factor_groups.std() / factor_groups.mean()
                    environmental_correlations[factor] = {
                        'variation': variation,
                        'groups': factor_groups.to_dict(),
                        'is_significant': variation > 0.3
                    }
        
        return {
            'correlations': environmental_correlations,
            'has_environmental_dependency': any(
                corr['is_significant'] 
                for corr in environmental_correlations.values()
            ),
            'suggested_fixes': self._generate_environmental_fixes(environmental_correlations)
        }

class AITestGenerator:
    """
    AI-powered test generation system.
    
    Generates test cases from:
    - Natural language requirements
    - Code analysis
    - API specifications
    - User stories
    - Existing test patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.model = self._load_test_generation_model()
        self.requirement_parser = RequirementParser()
        self.code_analyzer = CodeAnalyzer()
        
    def generate_tests_from_requirements(self, requirements: List[str], 
                                       context: Dict[str, Any] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Generate comprehensive test suite from natural language requirements.
        """
        
        generated_tests = {
            'positive_tests': [],
            'negative_tests': [],
            'edge_cases': [],
            'integration_tests': [],
            'performance_tests': []
        }
        
        for requirement in requirements:
            # Parse requirement using NLP
            parsed_requirement = self.requirement_parser.parse(requirement)
            
            # Generate test scenarios
            test_scenarios = self._generate_test_scenarios(parsed_requirement, context)
            
            # Categorize and enhance tests
            categorized_tests = self._categorize_tests(test_scenarios)
            
            # Add to generated tests
            for category, tests in categorized_tests.items():
                generated_tests[category].extend(tests)
        
        # Apply test design techniques
        generated_tests = self._apply_test_design_techniques(generated_tests)
        
        # Generate executable test code
        executable_code = self._generate_executable_code(generated_tests)
        
        # Calculate coverage metrics
        coverage_metrics = self._calculate_coverage_metrics(generated_tests, requirements)
        
        return {
            'requirements': requirements,
            'generated_tests': generated_tests,
            'executable_code': executable_code,
            'coverage_metrics': coverage_metrics,
            'test_data_requirements': self._generate_test_data_requirements(generated_tests),
            'validation_criteria': self._generate_validation_criteria(generated_tests)
        }
    
    def _generate_test_scenarios(self, parsed_requirement: Dict[str, Any],
                               context: Dict[str, Any] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Generate test scenarios from parsed requirements.
        """
        
        scenarios = []
        
        # Generate basic happy path scenarios
        happy_path_scenarios = self._generate_happy_path_scenarios(parsed_requirement)
        scenarios.extend(happy_path_scenarios)
        
        # Generate error/negative scenarios
        error_scenarios = self._generate_error_scenarios(parsed_requirement)
        scenarios.extend(error_scenarios)
        
        # Generate edge cases
        edge_cases = self._generate_edge_cases(parsed_requirement)
        scenarios.extend(edge_cases)
        
        # Apply context-specific scenarios
        if context:
            context_scenarios = self._generate_context_scenarios(parsed_requirement, context)
            scenarios.extend(context_scenarios)
        
        return scenarios
    
    def _apply_test_design_techniques(self, tests: Dict[str, List]) -> Dict[str, List]:
        """
        Apply test design techniques to enhance test coverage.
        """
        
        enhanced_tests = {}
        
        for category, test_list in tests.items():
            enhanced_category_tests = []
            
            for test in test_list:
                # Apply boundary value analysis
                boundary_tests = self._apply_boundary_value_analysis(test)
                enhanced_category_tests.extend(boundary_tests)
                
                # Apply equivalence partitioning
                equivalence_tests = self._apply_equivalence_partitioning(test)
                enhanced_category_tests.extend(equivalence_tests)
                
                # Apply decision table testing
                decision_tests = self._apply_decision_table_testing(test)
                enhanced_category_tests.extend(decision_tests)
                
                # Apply state transition testing
                state_tests = self._apply_state_transition_testing(test)
                enhanced_category_tests.extend(state_tests)
            
            enhanced_tests[category] = enhanced_category_tests
        
        return enhanced_tests

import pandas as pd

class IntelligentTestAnalytics:
    """
    Comprehensive test analytics system powered by AI and ML.
    
    Provides:
    - Predictive test failure analysis
    - Root cause identification
    - Anomaly detection
    - Performance optimization
    - Quality trend forecasting
    """
    
    def __init__(self, config: Dict[str, Any] = None):
        self.config = config or {
            'prediction_confidence_threshold': 0.7,
            'anomaly_detection_sensitivity': 0.1,

        }

        self.test_analytics_data = pd.DataFrame()
